claim: The hippocampal system appears to be critically important in establishing episodic memory of both internal and external events within contexts as well as spatial memory, which enables flexible spatial navigation.
source_text: The hippocampal system appears to be critically important in establishing episodic memory of both internal and external events within contexts as well as spatial memory, which enables flexible spatial navigation.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about hippocampal function based on prior research in the field.

claim: The neuronal substrates that function across different memories in the hippocampal system are poorly understood.
source_text: However, the neuronal substrates that function across different memories in the hippocampal system are poorly understood.
evidence_reasoning: This represents a gap in scientific knowledge acknowledged by the field prior to this study.

claim: The activity patterns of the hippocampal ensemble represent spatiotemporal contexts (journeys) constructed by temporally ordered past, present and expected future places in tandem with visually or mnemonically guided non-spatial contexts (task-demands) to form episodes.
source_text: I found that the activity patterns of the hippocampal ensemble represent spatiotemporal contexts (journeys) constructed by temporally ordered past, present and expected future places in tandem with visually or mnemonically guided non-spatial contexts (task-demands) to form episodes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding based on experimental observations from monitoring hippocampal neuronal ensembles in rats performing the task.

claim: The hierarchical organization of contexts based on pattern separation and completion enables the hippocampus to play a dual role in spatial navigation and recall of episodic memory.
source_text: This finding therefore suggests that the hierarchical organization of contexts based on pattern separation and completion enables the hippocampus to play a dual role in spatial navigation and recall of episodic memory.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings, inferring a functional mechanism from the observed activity patterns.

claim: Hippocampal pyramidal neurons discharge specifically at a certain location in the environment (the 'place field').
source_text: During spatial behaviors, hippocampal pyramidal neurons discharge specifically at a certain location in the environment (the 'place field'), suggesting that hippocampal neurons function in spatial memory
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from prior research, supported by citations to O'Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971; McNaughton and Morris, 1987; Muller et al., 1987.

claim: Episodic memory provides a record of past experiences in relation to a broad range of materials and is structured by spatial, temporal, and non-spatial contexts.
source_text: In contrast, episodic memory provides a record of past experiences in relation to a broad range of materials (Wood et al., 1999) and is structured by spatial, temporal, and non-spatial contexts (Tulving, 1983).
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations to Wood et al., 1999 and Tulving, 1983, representing established knowledge about episodic memory.

claim: The place field of a given neuron changes (remapping) relative to three different contexts: spatial context characterized by environmental features, spatiotemporal context (journey) affected by the experienced origin and expected destination, and internally and externally guided non-spatial context (task-demand).
source_text: Recent studies indicate that on the basis of the pattern separation and completion proposed by Marr (Marr, 1969), the place field of a given neuron changes (remapping) relative to three different contexts: spatial context characterized by environmental features (Bostock et al., 1991; Kentros et al., 1998), spatiotemporal context (journey) affected by the experienced origin and expected destination (Frank et al., 2000; Wood et al., 2000), and internally and externally guided non-spatial context (task-demand) (Gothard et al., 1996; Anderson and Jeffery, 2003; Smith and Mizumori, 2006).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from multiple prior studies, supported by several citations.

claim: During a temporal gap between events, place cells encode successive moments or fire at a specific part of an episode.
source_text: Moreover, during a temporal gap between events, the place cells encode successive moments or fire at a specific part of an episode (Pastalkova et al., 2008; MacDonald et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Pastalkova et al., 2008 and MacDonald et al., 2011.

claim: Ensemble activity was recorded from a total of 1119 pyramidal cells in the CA1 of the dorsal hippocampus using arrays of 10 extracellular dodecatrodes in five rats running in the maze.
source_text: Ensemble activity was recorded from a total of 1119 pyramidal cells in the CA1 of the dorsal hippocampus using arrays of 10 extracellular dodecatrodes (Takahashi and Sakurai, 2005) in five rats running in the maze.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental data collection methodology and sample size.

claim: All rats were familiarized with the task before recording, and performed the task with a high level of accuracy (overall: 99 ± 2%, VD: 99 ± 1%, SA: 97 ± 3%, DA: 99 ± 1% correctly performed).
source_text: All rats were familiarized with the task before recording, and performed the task with a high level of accuracy (overall: 99 ± 2%, VD: 99 ± 1%, SA: 97 ± 3%, DA: 99 ± 1% correctly performed [mean ± SEM]; Table 1).
evidence_reasoning: This presents quantitative behavioral performance data from the experiments.

claim: The hippocampal place code is influenced by running speed and head direction.
source_text: Several studies suggest that the hippocampal place code is influenced by running speed and head direction
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from prior studies, though specific citations are not provided in this sentence fragment.

claim: Different journeys in the same place resulted in place fields similar in locations, but different task-demands caused different firing intensities in those place fields.
source_text: Note that different journeys in the same place resulted in place fields similar in locations, but different task-demands caused different firing intensities in those place fields.
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Changes in both firing location and rates in the place field (global remapping) occurred between the different journeys.
source_text: Changes in both firing location and rates in the place field (global remapping) occurred between the different journeys.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a specific pattern observed in the experimental data regarding place field remapping.

claim: Only changes in the firing rates (rate remapping) occurred between the task-demands.
source_text: By contrast, only changes in the firing rates (rate remapping) occurred between the task-demands.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a specific pattern observed in the experimental data regarding place field remapping between task conditions.

claim: The spatial representation of the hippocampal CA1 at various points in the maze were dissimilar in both firing location and rate among different journeys, irrespective of either visually or mnemonically guided demands, in a global remapping manner.
source_text: To summarize, although the same prominent environmental features were encountered in the same locations, the spatial representation of the hippocampal CA1 at various points in the maze were dissimilar in both firing location and rate among different journeys, irrespective of either visually or mnemonically guided demands, in a global remapping manner.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of the primary experimental findings regarding place field remapping patterns.

claim: When the rats experienced changes in prominent, non-spatial features with internal and external events (i.e., subtask differences), the hippocampus only modulated the journey-dependent activity by primarily changing the intensity of the firing rates.
source_text: However, when the rats experienced changes in prominent, non-spatial features with internal and external events (i.e., subtask differences), the hippocampus only modulated the journey-dependent activity by primarily changing the intensity of the firing rates.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a specific experimental finding about how hippocampal activity changes with task demands.

claim: Neither the journey-dependent nor demand-specific coding was chiefly influenced by the running speed, head direction, or lateral position.
source_text: Neither the journey-dependent nor demand-specific coding was chiefly influenced by the running speed, head direction, or lateral position.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from statistical analysis controlling for these behavioral variables.

claim: Even when the given task-demands were different, the classifier could sufficiently predict the journey from the ensemble activity patterns, suggesting that the journey representation is generalized and that non-spatial demand-specific representation is hierarchically ranked at a lower level.
source_text: In addition to the evidence from the place field measurements, even when the given task-demands were different, the classifier could sufficiently predict the journey from the ensemble activity patterns, suggesting that the journey representation is generalized and that non-spatial demand-specific representation is hierarchically ranked at a lower level.
evidence_reasoning: This combines experimental results from classifier analysis with an interpretation about hierarchical organization.

claim: The neuronal trajectory of the ensemble activity differed enough to classify any trial type; prior to its behavioral choice, significant accuracy could be achieved even in a visually-guided situation in which memory-guided decision could not be made.
source_text: The neuronal trajectory of the ensemble activity differed enough to classify any trial type; prior to its behavioral choice, significant accuracy could be achieved even in a visually-guided situation in which memory-guided decision could not be made.
evidence_reasoning: This describes findings from the neuronal trajectory classification analysis.

claim: The neuronal ensemble code for distinguishing trial types in the hippocampal ensemble activity was relatively equal to that for journeys and task-demands.
source_text: The neuronal ensemble code for distinguishing trial types in the hippocampal ensemble activity was relatively equal to that for journeys and task-demands.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from comparing classification accuracies across different categories.

claim: Based not only on externally induced but also internally generated events, the hippocampus processes the combination of journey and task-demand as a single episode.
source_text: Thus, the results imply that based not only on externally induced but also internally generated events, the hippocampus processes the combination of journey and task-demand as a single episode.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings about how the hippocampus integrates different types of information.

claim: Hippocampal neurons might convey information related to where an animal is located (place-specific coding).
source_text: Previous studies have reported that hippocampal neurons might convey information related to where an animal is located (place-specific coding)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from prior research, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Hippocampal neurons might convey information related to where an animal had just been (retrospective coding).
source_text: Previous studies have reported that hippocampal neurons might convey information related to...where it had just been (retrospective coding)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from prior research, supported by citations to Frank et al., 2000; Wood et al., 2000; Ferbinteanu and Shapiro, 2003; Ferbinteanu et al., 2011.

claim: Hippocampal neurons might convey information related to where an animal is about to go next (prospective coding).
source_text: Previous studies have reported that hippocampal neurons might convey information related to...where it is about to go next (prospective coding)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from prior research, supported by citations to Frank et al., 2000; Wood et al., 2000; Ferbinteanu and Shapiro, 2003; Ainge et al., 2007a; Ferbinteanu et al., 2011.

claim: Hippocampal neurons might convey information related to what demand an animal currently faces (demand-specific coding).
source_text: Previous studies have reported that hippocampal neurons might convey information related to...what demand it currently faces (demand-specific coding)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from prior research, supported by citations to Gothard et al., 1996; Anderson and Jeffery, 2003; Smith and Mizumori, 2006.

claim: All of the information about place, past location, future location, and current demand can be simultaneously preserved in the hippocampal output to form episodes.
source_text: I report that all of this information can be simultaneously preserved in the hippocampal output to form episodes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding from the current study's experimental data.

claim: The information for journey and task-demand is not horizontally but hierarchically organized.
source_text: The information for journey and task-demand is not horizontally but hierarchically organized
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings about the organization of information in hippocampal activity.

claim: Expected future events in the hippocampus can trigger episode separation.
source_text: expected future events in the hippocampus can trigger episode separation.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation based on the experimental findings about neuronal trajectory changes.

claim: Journey and task-demand can be considered to be spatiotemporal and non-spatial contexts, respectively.
source_text: From the viewpoint of context, journey and task-demand can be considered to be spatiotemporal and non-spatial contexts, respectively.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conceptual interpretation of the experimental variables in terms of context theory.

claim: The hierarchical organization of spatiotemporal and non-spatial contexts in the hippocampal episodic code, which is based on the context version of pattern separation and completion through the remapping of place fields, not only enables flexible spatial navigation but also contributes to the recall of episodic memory.
source_text: Thus, the hierarchical organization of spatiotemporal and non-spatial contexts in the hippocampal episodic code, which is based on the context version of pattern separation and completion through the remapping of place fields, not only enables flexible spatial navigation but also contributes to the recall of episodic memory.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main conclusion of the study, integrating experimental findings with theoretical interpretation about hippocampal function.

claim: Five male Wister rats (300–400 g) were used in the study.
source_text: Five male Wister rats (300–400 g) were housed individually in cages (20 × 25 × 23 cm).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental subjects used in the study.

claim: All rats were implanted with a custom-made microdrive with 10 dodecatrodes and 2 reference electrodes.
source_text: All of them were implanted with a custom-made microdrive with 10 dodecatrodes and 2 reference electrodes.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental methodology for neural recording.

claim: The rats were kept at 80% of free-feeding body weight.
source_text: The rats were kept at 80% of free-feeding body weight.
evidence_reasoning: This describes an experimental condition used to motivate the animals.

claim: During immobility periods, including delay periods, hippocampal activity is not place-specific.
source_text: It is well known that during immobility periods, including delay periods, hippocampal activity is not place-specific (McNaughton et al., 1983; Pastalkova et al., 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge from prior research, supported by citations.

claim: The 10 dodecatrodes were lowered into the hippocampal CA1 pyramidal layer within 2 weeks of surgery.
source_text: The 10 dodecatrodes were lowered into the hippocampal CA1 pyramidal layer within 2 weeks of surgery.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental procedure for electrode placement.

claim: The optimal MFB stimulation consisted of a train of 2 ms wide, 100–200 μA, biphasic current pulses, delivered at 100 Hz for 200 ms.
source_text: The optimal MFB stimulation consisted of a train of 2 ms wide, 100–200 μA, biphasic current pulses, delivered at 100 Hz for 200 ms.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental parameters used for reward stimulation.

claim: The task was performed under dim light to prevent the rats from accessing unnecessary distal room cues.
source_text: To prevent the rats from accessing unnecessary distal room cues, the task was performed under dim light.
evidence_reasoning: This describes an experimental control condition.

claim: The rats did not access the visual cue until reaching the decision point because the height of the walls of the maze (20 cm) was much higher than the level of the rat's eyes (∼5 cm) and the rats did not stand up during the experiment.
source_text: The rats did not access the visual cue until reaching the decision point (Figure 1A) because the height of the walls of the maze (20 cm) was much higher than the level of the rat's eyes (∼5 cm) and the rats did not stand up during the experiment.
evidence_reasoning: This describes an experimental design feature and infers the rats' visual access based on physical measurements.

claim: Putative pyramidal cells were distinguished from putative fast spiking interneurons by the spike width (0.4 ms) and the average firing rate (5 Hz).
source_text: After spike sorting, putative pyramidal cells were distinguished from putative fast spiking interneurons by the spike width (0.4 ms) and the average firing rate (5 Hz).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the methodology for cell classification based on established electrophysiological criteria.

claim: Low rate cells (<0.1 Hz) were excluded from analysis.
source_text: The low rate cells (<0.1 Hz) were excluded.
evidence_reasoning: This describes an exclusion criterion applied in the data analysis.

claim: Spikes during immobility periods in the maze were excluded from analysis.
source_text: Thus, spikes during immobility periods in the maze were excluded.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a data processing step applied in the analysis.
